blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — From bird calls overhead to bats and reptiles tucked into their habitats, a two-day wildlife survey in Bohol’s Alburquerque-Loay-Loboc Protected Landscape and Seascape (ALLPLS) recorded 55 species across the protected area. The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Central Visayas said the monitoring on Sept. 15 and 16 documented 47 bird species, four bat species and four reptile species. The activity was part of the second-semester Biodiversity Assessment and Monitoring System fauna monitoring at ALLPLS, which covers 1,165.52 hectares across three municipalities and 23 barangays.
